subject: Abraham
note: Every Bible line on the page is the BSB, checked against shared/bsb-berean-standard-bible.txt by verify-quotes.mjs (research/people/abraham.quotes.json). Fathers from ANF 1 and 3 on disk; Josephus (Whiston), the Jewish Encyclopedia (1906), Budge's Paradise (1907), the OCA, the Coptic synaxarium and Schaff's Creeds fetched into sources/people/abraham/. Britannica read for the three faiths, the site of Ur and the first land he owned: paraphrased, never quoted.

life.text: Terah fathered Abram, Nahor and Haran; Haran died in Ur of the Chaldeans leaving Lot; Sarai was barren; Terah set out from Ur for Canaan but settled in Haran and died there at 205.
Terah and the fathers 'worshiped other gods' beyond the Euphrates.
Stephen: God appeared to Abraham in Mesopotamia before he lived in Haran; God gave him 'not even a foot of ground' as inheritance.
The call; left Haran at 75; altar at Shechem, then Bethel.
Egypt: 'say you are my sister'; plagues on Pharaoh's house; Pharaoh's rebuke. Repeated at Gerar with Abimelech; Abraham: she is his father's daughter, not his mother's.
Parting from Lot near Bethel; Lot chose the Jordan plain toward Sodom; Abram moved to the Oaks of Mamre at Hebron.
318 trained men; pursuit to Dan; Melchizedek king of Salem, priest of God Most High, bread and wine, a tenth; refused the king of Sodom's goods.
Count the stars; 'Abram believed the LORD, and it was credited to him as righteousness'; the covenant between the pieces, smoking firepot and flaming torch; 400 years of slavery foretold.
Hagar after ten years in Canaan; the angel at the spring on the road to Shur; 'You are the God who sees me'; Ishmael born when Abram was 86.
At 99: 'I am God Almighty'; Abram renamed Abraham, 'a father of many nations'; Sarai renamed Sarah; he laughed; circumcision the same day with Ishmael, 13.

Three men at the Oaks of Mamre; water, bread, a calf, curds and milk; Sarah laughed; 'Is anything too difficult for the LORD?'; the plea for Sodom from fifty down to ten; next morning the smoke; God 'remembered Abraham' and brought Lot out.
Isaac born when Abraham was 100; Sarah: 'God has made me laugh'; the feast at the weaning; Hagar and Ishmael sent away; the well; 'God was with the boy'; Ishmael a great archer.
Abimelech: 'God is with you in all that you do'; the oath at Beersheba.
The binding of Isaac on Moriah; the ram; 'The LORD Will Provide'. Hebrews: he reasoned God could raise the dead.
Sarah died at 127 at Hebron; the cave of Machpelah bought from Ephron for 400 shekels of silver.
The chief servant's oath; Rebekah; Isaac comforted after his mother's death.
Keturah and six sons; everything left to Isaac; died at 175 'old and contented'; Isaac and Ishmael buried him at Machpelah with Sarah.

Britannica: the first Hebrew patriarch, revered by Judaism, Christianity and Islam; Jews and Christians trace the promise through Isaac, Islam through Ishmael, of whom Muhammad is a descendant; most scholars place Ur Kasdim at the Sumerian Ur (Tall al-Muqayyar), about 300 km south-east of Baghdad; Machpelah 'the first clear ownership of a piece of the promised land'.
life.note: Paraphrased only; Britannica is not public domain.

life.text: OCA: he lived around 2000 BC; commemorated 9 October; also on the Sunday of the Holy Forefathers (11 to 17 December).

tidbits_and_numbers.text: First use of 'prophet' in the Bible is Genesis 20:7, of Abraham; first 'Hebrew' is Genesis 14:13, 'Abram the Hebrew'. Checked in the BSB file and in BDB as printed on Bible Hub (Strong's 5030 lists Genesis 20:7 first; 5680 lists Genesis 14:13 first).
'Friend' of God: 2 Chronicles 20:7, Isaiah 41:8, James 2:23: the only three BSB verses joining Abraham and friend.
Moriah appears twice in the BSB: Genesis 22:2 and 2 Chronicles 3:1 (Solomon's temple).
Numbers: 75 at leaving Haran (12:4) and 175 at death (25:7); 100 at Isaac's birth, Sarah 90 (17:17; 21:5); 318 men (14:14); 400 shekels (23:15-16).
Hebrews 11 gives Abraham verses 8-12 and 17-19, more than anyone else in the chapter.

fathers_and_later.text: 1 Clement 10: 'Abraham, styled "the friend," was found faithful...'; 'On account of his faith and hospitality, a son was given him in his old age'. 1 Clement 31: Isaac 'cheerfully yielded himself as a sacrifice'.
Barnabas 9: 318 read as IH (Jesus) and T (the cross). Not printed on the page in the end (the numbers column was full); kept here for a later tidbit.
Justin, Dialogue 56: He who appeared at Mamre is God, 'sent with the two angels in His company'.
Tertullian, An Answer to the Jews 10: Isaac bearing his own 'wood' pointed to Christ's death.
Abba Nastir: 'All rules of conduct are not alike. Abraham was a lover of strangers...'.
fathers_and_later.source: Budge, The Paradise of the Holy Fathers, vol. 2 (1907), Appendix, no. 605 (the same saying the personality test uses).

fathers_and_later.text: Josephus, Antiquities 1.7: left Chaldea at 75; 'the first that ventured to publish this notion, That there was but one God'. 1.8: taught the Egyptians arithmetic and astronomy. 1.13: 'Isaac was twenty-five years old'. 1.14: Sarah buried at Hebron. 1.17: 'a man of incomparable virtue'; died at 175, buried at Hebron by Isaac and Ishmael.
Josephus, Wars 4.9.7: the family's monuments at Hebron 'of the most excellent marble'; 'a very large turpentine tree' six furlongs from the city, said to have stood since creation.

The idol-shop legend (Genesis Rabbah 38; Tanna debe Eliyahu) and Jubilees' burning of the house of idols, as summarised in the Jewish Encyclopedia; JE dates Jubilees 'probably in the time of John Hyrcanus' (134-104 BC), hence 'second century BC'.

faith_and_works.text: Trent, Decree on Justification ch. 8 ('justified by faith, because faith is the beginning of human salvation...'; nothing preceding, 'whether faith or works', merits it) and ch. 10 ('faith co-operating with good works', quoting James 2:24).
faith_and_works.source: Schaff, Creeds of Christendom vol. 2 (OCR on disk).

faith_and_works.text: Westminster Confession 11.2: faith 'the alone instrument of justification; yet is it not alone in the person justified'.
faith_and_works.source: Schaff vol. 3 (OCR; checked as a scan).

faith_and_works.text: Longer Catechism, question 482: faith without love and good works 'is inactive and dead'.

calendars.text: Roman Martyrology (1916), 9 October: 'the commemoration of the holy patriarch Abraham, father of all believers.'
Litany of the Saints (Calendarium Romanum 1969): 'Patriarchae et Prophetae: Sancte Abraham, ora pro nobis; Sancte Moyses...' Abraham first.
OCA: 9 October with Righteous Lot; Sunday of the Forefathers ('especially the Patriarch Abraham'); Sunday before the Nativity lists 'the righteous Patriarch Abraham, son of Terah'.
Coptic: 28 Mesra, 'Our father Abraham' with Isaac and Jacob. 28 Mesra = 3 September (Mesra 30 is 5 September in every year of this century; the leap day falls in the epagomenal days after it).
Not in the Church of England calendar (cofe-calendar.txt) nor Lesser Feasts and Fasts 2022 (lff2022.txt: Abraham appears only in other people's entries).

could_not_verify: The date of Genesis Rabbah: not given by the Jewish Encyclopedia's entry, so the page gives none.
The Barnabas tidbit was cut for space, not for doubt.
The Greek and Russian synaxaria were not fetched; the page gives the OCA's 9 October and the Forefathers Sundays, and the 22 October old-calendar date is the 13-day arithmetic, as on Moses's page.
Whether the Hebron site today is the same as Josephus's monuments: not stated on the page.

Abba Nastir: 'asked what way of life a monk should follow' became 'asked what rule of life a man should follow', as Budge has it ('What rule of life and conduct should a man follow?').
Family fact: the comma stack on his sons made plain.
